correctness.rationale: The polynomial is grounded and has uniform univariate margins. The mixed derivative is 1+λ(1−2z)[1−2αx−2βy−4(1−α−β)xy]. The bracket is bilinear and is a convex interpolation of its four corner values, so the stated maximum gives both necessary and sufficient nonnegative density on the cube. Strict failure at a vertex forces negative density on a nearby interior box; equality is allowed. Writing s=α+β, the integral of xy[1−αx−βy−(1−s)xy] is (5−2s)/36 and the integral of z(1−z) is 1/6; this yields ρ=λ(5−2s)/27. At the midpoint the bracket before multiplication by (1−z) is (3−s)/4, so the stated normalization gives M=λ(3−s)/24. The linear map from (a,b) has determinant 1/1296. Given a≠0 and |a|,|b|≤1, α=β=(3+b/a)/4 realizes the point with other scaled corners both equal to −(a+b)/2. Finite parameters with a=0 force b=0. The joint positive and negative extrema occur uniquely at (a,b)=(1,−1) and (−1,1); translating the remaining corner bounds gives α+β=1 and both parameters in [0,1]. Thus the math of the stated finite-parameter image and sharp bounds is correct.
residual_risks: The proof uses nonnegative density, not strict positivity at every point; zeros at extreme parameters are allowed. The seeded probes in the frozen checker were not executed and are not needed for the universal proof.
